title: JFrog reference token in the X-JFrog-Art-Api header or as the basic-authentication password
summary: A synthetic value after X-JFrog-Art-Api in a raw request and a quoted curl -H argument, and as the password of a curl -u username:value pair.
rationale: JFrog documents that a reference token can be used like an API key in the X-JFrog-Art-Api header, or as basic credentials (curl -u User1:<reference token>), and that it is not retrievable after creation (contract claim carriers-and-handling). JFrog's two current pages state 64 and 128 characters and the evidence on the grammar after the cmVmd prefix is in conflict (length-64-versus-128-conflict), so no shape is used and the value is flagged because of where it sits. The extent is the value only: the header name, the user name and the separators are outside it. The same two slots are covered for API keys by jfrog-api-key-header-and-basic-password-value; this Case names the reference token family, and a header-only observation does not distinguish the two (open question api-key-and-other-token-boundary).

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the X-JFrog-Art-Api header or as the basic-authentication password of a JFrog request is treated as a credential whatever its shape. JFrog documents the header and the basic password as carriers of a reference token (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: reference tokens can be used similarly to API Keys , using the “ X-JFrog-Art-Api ” Header, or as basic credentials (“ curl -u User1:<reference token> ”).
sources.locator: Comparing Identity Reference Tokens With API Keys

sources.supports: A reference token can be used instead of a password for basic authentication.
